# Audio

* `synth/`: sounds generated by `tools/build_audio.py` (explosion, reload, "plip" cue, hit thud, helicopter loop). Ours; safe to commit.
* `local/`: **third-party material, not committed** (see `.gitignore`; `build.rs` packs it into the executable instead):
  gunshots and knife (from SoundEffectsFactory recordings), a distant gunfight bed, and the suspense music remixed
  from the track "La Misere Pa Douce" by Ti Roro (Lio S.A.).
  The owner says these may be used freely; keep the licences on file. Without these files the game still runs, silently.

Rebuild `local/` and `synth/` from the original recordings:

    WSR_AUDIO_SRC=/path/to/copies python3 tools/build_audio.py

(sources copied as ak.mp3, pistol.mp3, hmg.mp3, knife.mp3, pack.mp3, fight.mp3, voodoo.mp3).

Music: `music_calm.wav` and `music_tense.wav` are the same length and play together; the game crossfades with danger.
Press **M** in game to toggle the music. `suspense_showcase.wav` is a listening arrangement (calm, build, tense, calm), not used in game.

## Tuning

* `tools/meter.py` measures every sound (A-weighted loudness, peak, start/end clicks).
* `tools/simulate_mix.py` renders a busy firefight and a calm-to-tense crossfade with the game's real gains and reports clipping and balance.
  Last run: effects sit about 12 dB over the music in the heaviest fight; the crossfade stays within about 1 dB; worst-case clipping 0.01% of samples.
* Keys in game: **M** music on/off, **[** and **]** music volume, **,** and **.** effects volume.
* Loud sounds duck the music briefly; the calm layer carries mid-range body so it is audible on laptop speakers.

## Scarier music (2026-11-23)

`tools/scary_music.py` (Python 3 + ffmpeg, no numpy) layers dread onto both loops: tritone sub drone, binaural beating,
a sour minor-second "ghost" pair, breath/whisper noise, slow vibrato and long echoes (the tense loop gets more, plus a light bit-crush).
The untouched loops are kept in `local/orig/` and every run starts from them; loop length and seam are unchanged and loudness is matched to the originals.
I could not listen to it: check it by ear and adjust the numbers at the bottom of the script.

## Introduction music and kaleidoscope (2026-11-25)

`local/intro_mystery.wav` is a 61 s seamless loop that plays under the disclaimer and the story cards, over and over until ENTER
starts the game (slow fade-in, fade-out when play begins; **M** toggles it). It is remixed from a track the user supplied
("Djb andey pike 3 moun 36345450 - JÈNNVODOU GROUPE JERICHO 666 (st-marc jeanton1).mp3", a 21-minute ritual recording):

    python3 tools/intro_music.py /path/to/track.mp3 [start_seconds]      # default start 840 s, a steady stretch

Slowed 15 % (about -2.8 semitones), darkened, tape echo, 6 s synthetic reverb, a drone (A1, fifth, sour tritone, a soft 6 Hz binaural pair,
a minor-second shimmer), a slow "breathing" swell and auto-pan, mastered to about -26 LUFS (the game's music plays at about -17).
**Third-party recording: get permission and check the licence before release.** I could not listen to it; adjust the numbers at the top of the script by ear.

Research: dissonance, low drones, space (reverb, delay), silence and quiet sounds sprinkled in are supported by game-audio and music-psychology sources;
no source gave a loudness or reverb setting, and the "brain vibration" claims (binaural beats, infrasound) had no solid support.

The picture behind the cards is `src/kaleido.rs`: the `assets/veve` sigils in rings that turn slowly, mirrored, dissolving into each other.
